justification: Fresh read for the target query 'process vs thread' (CONTENT_PLAN.md section 7, angle C). I re-fetched the two top-ranking pages before opening any prior review. GeeksforGeeks: two illustrative, non-technical images, a nine-row comparison table, no runnable code, no measured numbers, explicitly 'introductory to intermediate' with no discussion of memory layout or scheduling. ByteByteGo: one unlabelled relationship diagram, five bullet differences, no code, no quantitative context-switch cost, no thread-pool or crash-isolation coverage. Baeldung returned HTTP 403 and could not be read. Against that bar this article's shell renders 20 real C# run blocks with distinct labelled 'C#'/Output panels, two hand-drawn figures, a two-column decision table, and four exercise callouts with collapsed solutions in a rhythm that alternates prose, code and figures every few paragraphs. I opened every desktop-light (14 parts + fold) and mobile-dark (22 parts + fold) screenshot, plus the fold and two interior parts each for desktop-dark and mobile-light, covering both figures in all four device/theme combinations. Everything I looked at, including the sections rewritten since round 1 ('What belongs to the process and what belongs to each thread', its Figure 1, and 'What a context switch costs'), renders cleanly: no overflow, no clipped labels, both diagrams legible and theme-correct at 390 px, the decision table needs no horizontal scroll, code blocks fade long boilerplate at the right edge while operative tokens (ProcessorAffinity, WaitOne/Set, atOnce) stay inside ~40 visible columns, and dark-mode contrast on callouts/diagrams is intact. verify-page (node tools/verify-page.mjs --drafts /operating-systems/processes-and-threads/) confirms the mechanics: Lighthouse 96/100/100/100, 0 console errors, 0 broken links (21 external, all resolved), 0 px mobile horizontal overflow, and only the expected NEEDS_MARKUS placeholder failure. That is a clear step above both re-read competing pages, consistent with round 1's independent finding of 9.0 (comparedAgainst GeeksforGeeks/ByteByteGo/MS Learn overview) -- I am not raising the score for effort, but the underlying design quality genuinely still clears the 8.5 'equal to MDN/Real Python' anchor by a comfortable margin without reaching the 10 'clearly better than best existing result with no nits' bar, because the shell's own Lighthouse performance sub-metrics still show avoidable headroom (see issue below), unchanged in kind since round 1. Note: other agents were active in this repo during this run (see git status), so the performance sub-score (96, versus round 1's 93) may be somewhat noisy; the orchestrator should treat it as indicative, not final, and re-measure serially if it matters to the gate.

Same shape of finding as round 1's issue; it has not been addressed and could be partly measurement noise from other agents sharing the machine during this run.

This does not block the round-2 pass bar for this critic (Lighthouse performance is 96, well above 90), so it remains a follow-up, not a blocker.
